value.body: Recruiters find, screen and line up candidates for open roles, either inside a company's HR team or at a staffing or search firm working for clients. A typical day involves reading job requirements, searching job portals and professional networks, phone-screening candidates, scheduling interviews and following up on offers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA, BA, B.Com or an MBA in HR

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Job portals, an applicant tracking system, Excel, LinkedIn

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: Talent acquisition executive, HR recruiter, sourcing associate

items.label: Formal flexi staff at ISF member firms
items.note: Covers only members of the federation, not all staffing work in India

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many freshers start as recruitment or sourcing executives at staffing firms, which hire graduates from most streams and train on the job. In-house talent acquisition roles more often ask for an HR specialisation, an MBA in HR or prior staffing experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Sourcing and screening candidates against a job description
Coordinating interviews and offers with hiring managers
Keeping candidate records in an applicant tracking system
Negotiating notice periods and joining dates

value.title: At a glance
items: Staffing-firm roles often carry monthly hiring targets.
Common next steps: senior recruiter, talent acquisition lead, or a broader HR business partner role.
Hiring demand rises and falls with the economy, so workload can swing.

competition.note: BBA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
